extracted.intended_audience: news organizations, editors, journalists, newsroom leaders seeking to adopt Trust Project standards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for news organizations on transparency, accuracy, and audience-facing trust practices defined by The Trust Project (the Trust Indicators) to demonstrate who and what is behind a news story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful, verified news and information in context
rubrics_metrics.description: Truthful, verified news and information in a context that gives them meaning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News partners strive to provide truthful, verified reporting and present information with context so audiences can understand significance. This reflects the Trust Project's mission to amplify transparency, accuracy, multiple perspectives and fairness so the public can make informed news choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forums for civil exchange and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Forums for civil exchanges and greater understanding of various viewpoints, with fairness in mind
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should provide spaces (forums) that encourage civil discourse and foster understanding across viewpoints, ensuring fairness in moderation and presentation of differing perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect diverse communities and interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories, information and ideas that reflect diverse types of communities and their interests and views
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial choices should include coverage and viewpoints representing a range of communities and interests, avoiding narrow or monolithic perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold the public interest and hold power accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Uphold the public’s interest, which includes holding the powerful accountable and shining a light in unexpected places
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism should serve the public interest by investigating and reporting on power structures, including stories that may be overlooked but are important for accountability and civic awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and accuracy (including prompt corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness and accuracy. Publishing corrections or clarifications as promptly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must prioritize accurate reporting and fairness; when errors occur they should publish corrections or clarifications promptly. This is an explicit Trust Indicator commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures of mission, funding, and organizational identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures that explain our mission, source(s) of funding and the organization behind us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News outlets should be transparent about their mission and funding sources and clearly identify the organization producing the content so audiences can evaluate potential conflicts or biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insight into methods and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Insight into our methods and where we get our information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide audience-facing explanations of reporting methods, how information was obtained, and source practices so readers understand how conclusions were reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of voices and perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: A diversity of voices and perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively include multiple voices and viewpoints in coverage and indicate when a range of perspectives has been sought; this is presented separately as a Trust Indicator reinforcing inclusive reporting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for public engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and maintain channels for the public to engage with reporting (comments, feedback, Q&A, events), making it easy for audiences to participate and for newsrooms to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display the 8 Trust Indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Together and individually, the 8 Trust Indicators show who and what is behind a news story so people can easily assess for themselves whether it comes from a reliable source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should adopt and display the Trust Indicators on stories/sites to make provenance, methods, corrections, funding, and other trust-relevant information visible to audiences; The Trust Project invites organizations to apply to join and use these Indicators to build credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority (value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority: We base our work on research, evidence and the core ideals of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial work should be grounded in research and evidence and align with journalism's core ideals; this value signals the need for expertise, sourcing, and rigorous standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity (value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticity: We are truthful and follow strict standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to truthfulness and internal standards of verification and ethical practice; authenticity includes adherence to newsroom policies that ensure accuracy and honesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency: We are open, honest and accessible. We Illuminate, not obfuscate, and admit our mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about decision-making, sourcing, funding and errors; prioritize accessibility of information about how journalism is produced and correct mistakes publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity (value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusivity: Our work keeps a diverse public at its center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center diverse audiences and communities in coverage and newsroom practice, ensuring representation and consideration of varied needs and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness (value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness: Our work is impartial and respectful of differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice impartial reporting and respectful treatment of subjects and audiences; fairness is both an editorial stance and a practical standard for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability (value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability: We are consistent – and can be counted on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent standards and practices so audiences can depend on the organization over time; reliability includes consistent correction policies, sourcing practices, and clear presentation.
